notes.decision: Variant orthography of ⲙⲁⲛⲭⲗⲟⲡⲉ 'place of deceit' (already in accumulated vocab). The double-vowel ⲟⲟ is a Lycopolitan scribal expansion. Translated identically as 'places of deceit.'

Greek/Latin loanword φόσσα/fossa 'trench, ditch.' In Manichaean cosmology these are the three cosmic 'fossae' — pits/trenches prepared for the binding of the dark powers, paralleling the Three Ditches motif found in Manichaean cosmogony. Translated 'fossae' to preserve the technical specificity.

From ⲥⲱⲛϩ̄ 'to bind, to chain' (Lyc. ⲍ for ϩ). With 3pl object suffix and ⲛ̄ⲍⲏⲧⲟⲩ 'within them' = 'chain them within them.' Distinct from ⲥⲁⲛⲟⲩϣ 'nourish' (different root). The doublet 'bind (ⲙⲁⲣⲟⲩ) and chain (ⲥⲁⲛⲍⲟⲩ)' is the standard binding-imprisonment idiom for the dark powers in the fossae.
Greek πεῖρας 'limit, boundary' + 'of the sea.' The cosmic boundary of the great sea (cf. Job 38:8-11). The text describes a primordial moment before this boundary was established.

Likely Greek τοῖχος 'wall.' The Father of Life sets a cosmic wall in the great sea — the bounding structure that contains it. Could alternatively be τόπος 'place' but the phrasing 'a τόπος in the great sea' is less naturally cosmological than 'a wall in the great sea.'
'Father of Life' (ⲡⲧⲱⲛⲍ̄ = ⲡⲱⲛϩ 'Life'). Distinct cosmological figure paired with the Mother of Life; cf. accumulated vocab where ⲡⲓⲱⲧ ⲛ̄ⲧⲉ ⲡⲧⲱⲛⲍ̄ appears alongside ⲧⲙⲁⲩ ⲛ̄ⲧⲉ ⲡⲱⲛⲍ̄.

Plural of ⲥⲟⲃⲧⲉ 'preparation, defenses, prepared structures.' Translated 'prepared structures' to capture the construction-language; could also be 'enclosures' or 'fortifications' bounding the cosmic sea.
Likely ⲙⲟⲩϩ 'fullness' or 'completion' (Lyc. ⲍ for ϩ). The 'fullness within' the cosmic sea where the ships sail. Could alternatively be a derivative of ⲙⲟⲩϩⲉ 'fire-light.' Confidence moderate.

Greek ἐνθύμησις with feminine possessive ⲧⲉϩ- 'her': 'her Enthumesis' / 'the Enthumesis.' Already in accumulated vocab as a personified cosmic Thought operating in the realm of darkness — Hyle's reflective faculty. The 'sea of the Enthumesis' is the cosmic-watery medium of dark thinking.

'Palamas of the Light' (already in accumulated vocab). The cosmic figure who beckons after Matter/the Enthumesis. Translated 'Palamas' (transliterated, retaining Greek παλαμᾶσθαι 'to contrive') to preserve the technical specificity.

Tentative reading 'he hurled her.' Possibly from ⲛⲟⲩⲭ/ⲛⲟⲩϫⲉ 'cast, throw' with 3sg.f object. Could alternatively be 'he stretched her' or 'he cast her down.' The action is performed upon Matter (feminine) by the Father of Life (or the Palamas).

'The dregs of the Darkness' (tentative). ⲍⲁϩⲉ likely Lyc. reflex of ϩⲁⲏ 'rear, end, last part.' Paired with ⲡⲥⲁⲣⲙⲉ 'Error' as another negative cosmic principle being driven forth from creation. Could alternatively be 'the host/army of Darkness' or 'the rear-guard of Darkness.'

Lexeme uncertain. Possibly a class of dark beings or 'garments/coverings' that are 'clothed' (ⲃⲱⲟⲥ) in the archontic host. Could be related to ⲃⲉⲝ 'force, oppression' or a Greek loanword. Left transliterated and flagged.

Greek κνέφας 'darkness, twilight gloom' or κνώψ 'noxious creeping creature.' Given the inventory continues with clouds, winds, spirits, birds, the creature-reading 'dark beasts' fits the cosmic-fauna catalogue. Confidence moderate.
Lyc. plural form of ϩⲁⲗⲏⲧ 'bird' (cf. accumulated vocab ⲍⲛⲍⲁⲗⲗⲉⲧⲉ 'birds'). Translated 'birds' as the final member of the cosmic creature inventory.

Likely Greek ἀνώγαιον / ἀνώγειον 'upper room, upper place' (cf. Mark 14:15, Luke 22:12). The 'seven of the upper place' = the seven firmaments. Could alternatively be πανδοχεῖον 'inn, dwelling-place' but 'upper-place' fits the cosmological context better.

Tentative reading as 'pit/abyss' — possibly Lyc. variant or scribal error for ⲡϣⲓⲭϩ 'abyss' (already in accumulated vocab). Could alternatively be ⲡⲱϫϩ 'split, break.' Translated 'the abyss' tentatively.

'Abortions' (in accumulated vocab) — the archonic abortions falling from heaven before Adam's fashioning, a Manichaean cosmogonic motif paralleling the Enochic fallen Watchers tradition. Standard cosmic-mythological reference.
